title: Edge cardinality filter (Bloom/Sketch) protector for inference KPIs
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Problem: Some tenants and SDK integrations are generating high-cardinality label values at the edge (session_id, ephemeral trace tags, user_agent fragments). This causes unbounded cardinality when metrics are forwarded to Prometheus/long-term stores and leads to OOMs and billing spikes. Existing ingest-side sampling reduces volume but is reactive and costly for very spiky customers.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, deterministic, memory-bounded cardinality filter in the edge telemetry proxy/sidecar that detects label fields crossing per-tenant cardinality budgets and applies well-defined mitigation strategies before metrics hit the central ingest pipeline. The component must integrate with both OTLP (metrics & exemplars) and Prometheus push-style inputs, preserve diagnosability (exemplar + trace_id linkage) where possible, and emit observability about the mitigation actions.

Scope and design decisions: 
- Filter algorithms under consideration: Count-Min Sketch (CMS) for frequency detection vs. Bloom/Stable Bloom Filter for novelty detection. CMS chosen as primary for frequency estimation and memory-accuracy trade-off; Bloom used as a fast path for very low-memory edge devices.
- Per-edge memory budget: default 4MB per collector (configurable via sidecar config). Must support a smaller 512KB mode for tiny gateways.
- Tenant-aware buckets: maintain separate sketch per tenant_id or tenant hash; evict/compact sketches for inactive tenants after N minutes.
- Label focus: initial rollout targets high-risk keys: request_id/session_id, raw_user_agent, freeform_tags -> configured list via deploy-time policy.
- Mitigation strategies (in order): 
  1) Label contraction: replace full value with stable hash prefix + "[truncated]" for safety. 
  2) Cardinality-tier fallback: move metric to a coarser aggregation label (e.g., route->route_group) if available. 
  3) Drop label/value pair on metric exports but increment a dropped_label counter and attach exemplar with trace_id to the first dropped sample in a window for debugging.
- Exemplar handling: when dropping or contracting values, preserve a sampled exemplar that references the original trace/span ID so customers can backtrace problematic requests without exposing raw high-cardinality strings to the aggregator. Exemplar rate limit: 1 exemplar/tenant/10s by default.
- Compatibility: Must accept both OTLP MetricData (preferred) and Prometheus remote_write / Pushgateway inputs. For Prometheus pulls, the exporter agent should perform equivalently by mutating samples before remote_write.
- Telemetry: expose metrics emitted by the sidecar: cardinality_estimate{tenant, key}, dropped_labels_total{tenant, key, reason}, contraction_actions_total, sketch_memory_bytes{mode}. Also emit structured audit events for policy decisions to the local audit log (rotated).

Acceptance criteria: 
- Edge sidecar keeps steady max memory usage below configured budget in synthetic load tests (4MB and 512KB modes).
- Under a synthetic workload generating 1M unique values/min for a tenant, the central ingest does not increase unique label series by >0.5% compared to baseline controlled test.
- Exemplars are preserved in at least 95% of first-missed cases and contain valid trace_id links to end-to-end traces.
- Billing/test alerts: dropped_labels_total triggers SLO page when it exceeds configured threshold; dashboards show per-tenant mitigation events.
- Unit and integration tests for CMS correctness, eviction behavior, and Prometheus mutator are present in repo and pass CI.

Implementation plan: 
1) Prototype CMS-based library in telemetry/common (golang, small footprint) with deterministic hashing and optional stable bloom fallback. Benchmark memory/accuracy with replayed production label distributions (see dataset: gs://redwood-telemetry/label-samples/2026-01).
2) Implement sidecar integration layer: config flags, per-tenant table, eviction/TTL worker, exemplar preservation hooks.
3) Add Prometheus mutator pipeline to the push/remote_write adapter so both OTLP and Prometheus paths hit the same contraction logic.
4) Instrument and expose sidecar metrics and audit events; build Grafana panels for per-tenant mitigation heatmaps and a central mitigation timeline.
5) Canary rollout: opt-in tenants (internal + 3 high-volume customers) for 2 weeks, run smoke checks and inspect dropped labels dashboard.
6) Gradual rollout with default-off for public tenants; document config knobs in telem/ops runbook.

Trade-offs and notes: 
- False positives: sketch estimates may occasionally mark a rare valid label as high-cardinality; exemplar-based debugging and hash-prefix contraction mitigate loss of debuggability.
- Privacy: contraction + exemplar retention policy must be aligned with data retention rules; exemplar links may contain trace IDs that reference user data — operators must ensure trace retention policies are honored.
- Operational cost: additional CPU cost on edge collectors; we will monitor CPU/latency delta in canary.

Artifacts and links: 
- RFC: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/TELEMETRY/Edge+Cardinality+Filter+RFC (draft)
- Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-proto/pulls/114
- Benchmark notebook: https://notebooks.redwood.com/telemetry/cms-bench-2026-02.ipynb
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/edge-cardinality/canary-views
comments: 2026-02-22 - Liam O'Connor: Initial spike complete. CMS implementation shows good error bounds vs memory on replayed traffic. Prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-proto/pull/114

2026-02-27 - Maya Chen: Implemented per-tenant eviction and TTL worker. Observed edge CPU delta +4% in 4MB mode under load; acceptable for most hosts. Added config knob to disable exemplar preservation for tiny gateways.

2026-03-02 - PM review (R. Patel): Please ensure SRE runbook includes steps for emergency disable and how to correlate dropped_labels_total with customer tickets. Also add a toggle for contraction vs drop policy per tenant.

2026-03-04 - Security review (A. Gomez): Confirmed exemplar trace_id usage is compliant with retention policy when exemplars reference traces stored longer. No PII shipped in exemplars as we only store trace_id and timestamp. Will require opt-in until legal signs off.
2026-03-06 - QA: Integration tests added for Prometheus remote_write path. Found edge-case where histogram buckets were mutated incorrectly; fixed bucket-preserve path in PR #118.

2026-03-08 - Maya Chen: Canary started for internal tenants (tenant-infra, tenant-payments). Early dashboard shows contraction_actions_total increasing for tenant-payments correlated to a mobile SDK bug. Opened follow-up ENG bug: ENG-284161 to fix SDK value encoding.
